title: Reading an evolutionary tree
caption: Relatedness is shown by how recently two taxa share a common ancestor. The lizard and mouse share an ancestor that the frog does not, so they are more closely related to each other than either is to the frog. Each numbered trait arose once, on the branch shown, and is shared by every taxon above it.
alt: A tree of lancelet, shark, frog, lizard and mouse with five numbered traits on branches: vertebral column, jaws, four limbs, amniotic egg, and hair and mammary glands.
description: Branches are lineages, nodes are common ancestors and the tips are the taxa.
Trait 1, a vertebral column, and trait 2, jaws, arose in the ancestor of the shark, frog, lizard and mouse; the lancelet lacks them.
Trait 3, four limbs, arose in the ancestor of the frog, lizard and mouse; trait 4, the amniotic egg, in the ancestor of the lizard and mouse; trait 5, hair and mammary glands, in the mouse lineage.
The lizard and mouse share a more recent common ancestor with each other than with the frog.
